title: 03. Data Prep & Feature Engineering: Pipeline & Workflow Automation
summary: Pipeline and workflow automation are essential techniques for building robust, maintainable, and production-ready machine learning systems.

sections.title: Overview
sections.body: Pipeline and workflow automation are essential techniques for building robust, maintainable, and production-ready machine learning systems. These techniques help standardize the machine learning workflow, prevent data leakage, ensure reproducibility, and make models easier to deploy and maintain. Proper pipeline design is crucial for building scalable and reliable machine learning applications.

diagrams.title: fit / transform / predict inside a Pipeline
diagrams.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  subgraph TR["Training data"]
    f1["imputer.fit_transform"] --> f2["scaler.fit_transform"] --> f3["model.fit"]
  end
  subgraph NEW["Validation, test, production"]
    t1["imputer.transform"] --> t2["scaler.transform"] --> t3["model.predict"]
  end
  TR -.->|"same learned parameters"| NEW
diagrams.explain: fit learns parameters, transform applies them, fit_transform does both on training data. New data must only be transformed with the parameters learned in training. A Pipeline bundles the steps so cross-validation refits everything per fold and production applies exactly the same preprocessing.

sections.title: Why Pipeline Automation Matters
sections.body:
### 1. Data Leakage Prevention
- **Consistent Preprocessing**: Ensures same transformations applied to training and test data
- **Cross-Validation Safety**: Prevents information leakage during validation
- **Production Consistency**: Guarantees same preprocessing in production

### 2. Reproducibility
- **Standardized Workflow**: Consistent steps across different runs
- **Version Control**: Easy to track changes and rollback
- **Documentation**: Self-documenting code through pipeline structure

### 3. Maintainability
- **Modular Design**: Easy to modify individual components
- **Testing**: Simplified unit testing of pipeline components
- **Debugging**: Easier to identify and fix issues

### 4. Production Readiness
- **Deployment**: Easy to deploy entire pipeline as a unit
- **Monitoring**: Simplified monitoring of pipeline components
- **Scaling**: Easier to scale and parallelize

sections.title: Core Pipeline Components
sections.body:
### 1. Scikit-learn Pipeline

The Pipeline class chains multiple estimators into a single estimator, ensuring that preprocessing steps are applied consistently.

#### How Pipeline Works
1. **Sequential Execution**: Steps are executed in order
2. **Consistent Interface**: Pipeline behaves like a single estimator
3. **Data Flow**: Output of one step becomes input to the next
4. **Parameter Access**: Can access parameters of any step

#### Key Features
- **fit()**: Trains all steps in sequence
- **transform()**: Applies all transformations
- **predict()**: Makes predictions through entire pipeline
- **score()**: Evaluates pipeline performance
- **get_params()/set_params()**: Parameter management

#### Advantages
- **Data Leakage Prevention**: Ensures consistent preprocessing
- **Cross-Validation Safety**: Safe to use with cross-validation
- **Parameter Tuning**: Can tune parameters of any step
- **Simplified Interface**: Single estimator interface

#### When to Use
- When you have multiple preprocessing steps
- When using cross-validation
- When deploying models to production
- When you need reproducible workflows

### 2. FeatureUnion

FeatureUnion combines multiple feature extraction transformers into a single transformer, allowing parallel feature extraction.

#### How FeatureUnion Works
1. **Parallel Processing**: Multiple transformers run in parallel
2. **Feature Concatenation**: Results are concatenated horizontally
3. **Independent Transformers**: Each transformer operates independently
4. **Consistent Interface**: Behaves like a single transformer

#### Key Features
- **Parallel Execution**: Multiple transformers run simultaneously
- **Feature Concatenation**: Combines features from different sources
- **Independent Steps**: Each transformer can be different
- **Flexible Design**: Can combine any number of transformers

#### Advantages
- **Feature Diversity**: Combines different types of features
- **Parallel Processing**: Can improve performance
- **Modular Design**: Easy to add/remove feature extractors
- **Flexibility**: Can handle different data types

#### When to Use
- When you have multiple feature extraction methods
- When features come from different sources
- When you want to combine different data types
- When you need parallel feature processing

### 3. ColumnTransformer

ColumnTransformer applies different transformers to different columns of the data, allowing for column-specific preprocessing.

#### How ColumnTransformer Works
1. **Column Selection**: Selects specific columns for each transformer
2. **Parallel Processing**: Applies transformers to selected columns
3. **Feature Concatenation**: Combines results from all transformers
4. **Sparse Matrix Support**: Handles sparse matrices efficiently

#### Key Features
- **Column-Specific Processing**: Different preprocessing for different columns
- **Parallel Execution**: Multiple transformers run in parallel
- **Sparse Matrix Support**: Efficient handling of sparse data
- **Missing Value Handling**: Can handle missing values appropriately

#### Advantages
- **Heterogeneous Data**: Handles different data types efficiently
- **Performance**: Parallel processing improves speed
- **Memory Efficiency**: Sparse matrix support reduces memory usage
- **Flexibility**: Can handle any combination of column types

#### When to Use
- When you have mixed data types (numerical, categorical, text)
- When different columns need different preprocessing
- When you want to handle missing values differently
- When you need efficient sparse matrix processing

sections.title: Advanced Pipeline Techniques
sections.body:
### 1. Nested Pipelines

Nested pipelines allow you to create complex workflows with multiple levels of processing.

#### Structure
```python
pipeline = Pipeline([
    ('preprocessing', ColumnTransformer([
        ('num', Pipeline([('imputer', SimpleImputer()), ('scaler', StandardScaler())]), numerical_features),
        ('cat', Pipeline([('imputer', SimpleImputer(strategy='most_frequent')), ('encoder', OneHotEncoder())]), categorical_features)
    ])),
    ('classifier', RandomForestClassifier())
])
```

#### Advantages
- **Complex Workflows**: Handle sophisticated preprocessing needs
- **Modularity**: Easy to modify individual components
- **Reusability**: Can reuse pipeline components
- **Clarity**: Clear structure of the workflow

### 2. Custom Transformers

Custom transformers allow you to create specialized preprocessing steps.

#### Implementation
```python
class CustomTransformer(BaseEstimator, TransformerMixin):
    def __init__(self, param1=1.0):
        self.param1 = param1
    
    def fit(self, X, y=None):
        # Learn parameters from X
        return self
    
    def transform(self, X):

        return transformed_X
```

#### Advantages
- **Domain-Specific Logic**: Implement domain-specific preprocessing
- **Integration**: Seamlessly integrate with scikit-learn
- **Testing**: Easy to test individual components
- **Flexibility**: Can implement any transformation logic

### 3. Pipeline Persistence

Pipeline persistence allows you to save and load entire pipelines.

#### Methods
- **pickle**: Simple serialization
- **joblib**: Optimized for large objects
- **Custom Formats**: JSON, YAML for human-readable formats

#### Advantages
- **Model Deployment**: Easy to deploy complete pipelines
- **Version Control**: Track pipeline versions
- **Reproducibility**: Ensure exact same pipeline in production
- **Sharing**: Share pipelines across teams

sections.title: Best Practices
sections.body:
### 1. Pipeline Design

#### Modularity
- **Single Responsibility**: Each step should have one clear purpose
- **Reusability**: Design steps to be reusable across projects
- **Testability**: Make steps easy to test independently
- **Documentation**: Document the purpose and behavior of each step

#### Error Handling
- **Input Validation**: Validate inputs at each step
- **Graceful Degradation**: Handle errors gracefully
- **Logging**: Log important events and errors
- **Monitoring**: Monitor pipeline performance and errors

#### Performance
- **Efficient Transformers**: Use efficient implementations
- **Parallel Processing**: Use parallel processing where possible
- **Memory Management**: Manage memory usage carefully
- **Caching**: Cache intermediate results when appropriate

### 2. Data Flow Management

#### Data Validation
- **Schema Validation**: Validate data schema at each step
- **Type Checking**: Ensure correct data types
- **Range Validation**: Check for reasonable value ranges
- **Consistency Checks**: Ensure data consistency

#### State Management
- **Fitted State**: Ensure transformers are properly fitted
- **Parameter Persistence**: Save and restore transformer parameters
- **State Validation**: Validate pipeline state before use
- **Error Recovery**: Recover from state errors gracefully

### 3. Production Considerations

#### Deployment
- **Containerization**: Use containers for consistent deployment
- **Versioning**: Version pipelines and dependencies
- **Rollback**: Plan for pipeline rollback
- **Monitoring**: Monitor pipeline performance in production

#### Scaling
- **Horizontal Scaling**: Scale pipelines horizontally
- **Resource Management**: Manage computational resources
- **Load Balancing**: Balance load across multiple instances
- **Caching**: Cache results to improve performance

sections.title: Common Pipeline Patterns
sections.body:
### 1. Classification Pipeline

#### Basic Pattern
```python
pipeline = Pipeline([
    ('preprocessor', ColumnTransformer([
        ('num', StandardScaler(), numerical_features),
        ('cat', OneHotEncoder(), categorical_features)
    ])),
    ('classifier', RandomForestClassifier())
])
```

#### Advanced Pattern
```python
pipeline = Pipeline([
    ('preprocessor', ColumnTransformer([
        ('num', Pipeline([
            ('imputer', SimpleImputer(strategy='median')),
            ('scaler', StandardScaler())
        ]), numerical_features),
        ('cat', Pipeline([
            ('imputer', SimpleImputer(strategy='most_frequent')),
            ('encoder', OneHotEncoder(drop='first'))
        ]), categorical_features)
    ])),
    ('feature_selector', SelectKBest(k=10)),
    ('classifier', RandomForestClassifier())
])
```

### 2. Regression Pipeline

#### Basic Pattern
```python
pipeline = Pipeline([
    ('preprocessor', StandardScaler()),
    ('regressor', LinearRegression())
])
```

#### Advanced Pattern
```python
pipeline = Pipeline([
    ('preprocessor', ColumnTransformer([
        ('num', Pipeline([
            ('imputer', SimpleImputer(strategy='mean')),
            ('scaler', RobustScaler())
        ]), numerical_features),
        ('cat', Pipeline([
            ('imputer', SimpleImputer(strategy='constant', fill_value='missing')),
            ('encoder', TargetEncoder())
        ]), categorical_features)
    ])),
    ('regressor', GradientBoostingRegressor())
])
```

### 3. Text Processing Pipeline

#### Basic Pattern
```python
pipeline = Pipeline([
    ('vectorizer', TfidfVectorizer()),
    ('classifier', MultinomialNB())
])
```

#### Advanced Pattern
```python
pipeline = Pipeline([
    ('preprocessor', ColumnTransformer([
        ('text', Pipeline([
            ('vectorizer', TfidfVectorizer(max_features=1000)),
            ('feature_selector', SelectKBest(k=500))
        ]), text_features),
        ('metadata', Pipeline([
            ('imputer', SimpleImputer(strategy='median')),
            ('scaler', StandardScaler())
        ]), metadata_features)
    ])),
    ('classifier', RandomForestClassifier())
])
```

sections.title: Workflow Automation
sections.body:
### 1. Automated Pipeline Construction

#### Feature Detection
- **Data Type Detection**: Automatically detect data types
- **Missing Value Detection**: Identify missing value patterns
- **Outlier Detection**: Detect outliers automatically
- **Feature Importance**: Estimate feature importance

#### Pipeline Generation
- **Rule-Based**: Use rules to generate pipelines
- **Optimization-Based**: Optimize pipeline structure
- **Learning-Based**: Learn optimal pipeline structure
- **Template-Based**: Use templates for common patterns

### 2. Hyperparameter Optimization

#### Pipeline-Level Optimization
- **Grid Search**: Search through parameter combinations
- **Random Search**: Random parameter sampling
- **Bayesian Optimization**: Use Bayesian methods for optimization
- **Multi-Objective**: Optimize multiple objectives

#### Component-Level Optimization
- **Individual Tuning**: Tune each component separately
- **Joint Tuning**: Tune components together
- **Sequential Tuning**: Tune components in sequence
- **Adaptive Tuning**: Adapt tuning based on performance

### 3. Automated Model Selection

#### Model Comparison
- **Performance Metrics**: Compare models using multiple metrics
- **Statistical Testing**: Use statistical tests for comparison
- **Cross-Validation**: Use cross-validation for reliable comparison
- **Ensemble Methods**: Combine multiple models

#### Selection Criteria
- **Performance**: Select based on performance metrics
- **Complexity**: Consider model complexity
- **Interpretability**: Consider interpretability requirements
- **Deployment**: Consider deployment constraints

sections.title: Common Pitfalls
sections.body:
### 1. Data Leakage

#### Problem
- **Using Test Data**: Using test data for preprocessing decisions
- **Cross-Validation Issues**: Not handling cross-validation properly
- **Feature Engineering**: Using future information for feature engineering

#### Solutions
- **Proper Pipeline Design**: Use pipelines to prevent leakage
- **Cross-Validation**: Use proper cross-validation techniques
- **Data Splitting**: Split data before any preprocessing

### 2. Overfitting

#### Problem
- **Complex Pipelines**: Overly complex pipeline structures
- **Too Many Features**: Too many features relative to data size
- **Insufficient Validation**: Not enough validation

#### Solutions
- **Regularization**: Use regularization techniques
- **Feature Selection**: Select relevant features
- **Cross-Validation**: Use proper cross-validation

### 3. Performance Issues

#### Problem
- **Inefficient Transformers**: Using inefficient preprocessing steps
- **Memory Issues**: High memory usage
- **Slow Execution**: Slow pipeline execution

#### Solutions
- **Optimized Transformers**: Use optimized implementations
- **Memory Management**: Manage memory usage
- **Parallel Processing**: Use parallel processing where possible

### 4. Maintenance Issues

#### Problem
- **Complex Dependencies**: Complex dependency management
- **Version Conflicts**: Version conflicts between components
- **Documentation**: Poor documentation

#### Solutions
- **Modular Design**: Use modular pipeline design
- **Version Management**: Manage versions carefully
- **Documentation**: Maintain good documentation
